clue.text: Cretan botched an easy gallop

indicators.note: something botched is messed up, so the letters of the Greek islander are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clumsy islander from Crete ruins what should have been a gentle ride on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched' rearranges the six letters of CRETAN; 'an' simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's three-beat pace slower than a full gallop is this relaxed gait.

clue.text: Tom has a curry in the vault

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
to curry a horse is to groom it with a comb

explanation.surface: A man called Tom eats a spicy dish down in a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' is not food here: to curry a horse is to comb it, giving COMB after CAT and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground burial chamber or tunnel is a kind of vault for the dead.

clue.text: Unexpected demand for card game

parts.note: something unexpected is new, never seen before
demand for goods is a market for them

explanation.surface: A sudden call for a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWMARKET is an old British gambling card game, named like the Suffolk horseracing town.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a gambling game played with a standard pack, also called Michigan in the US.

clue.text: Island where small breed is raised with energy

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it to read upwards, so the dog breed is reversed

parts.note: a toy is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A place where little dogs are reared vigorously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is raised' turns TOY upwards to YOT; E is placed before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small islet in a river, especially the Thames, is a type of island.

clue.text: Notice about sound of clock found in kitchen

indicators.note: the word for notice is placed around the clock sound, surrounding it

parts.note: to notice something is to spot it
tick-tock: the tock is a clock's sound

explanation.surface: Someone spots a clock ticking away in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps SPOT round TOCK, splitting it as S-TOCK-POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deep pan for simmering broth sits on most kitchen stoves.

clue.text: Smart volunteers take lactic compound

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: a compound mixes ingredients together, so the letters of the acid's name are mixed

explanation.surface: Clever volunteers swallow a chemical made from lactic acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' rearranges LACTIC to CTICAL, set after TA. The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, cleverly calculated moves can be described as both of these.

clue.text: Prince's not getting up for the dance

parts.note: Charles was the long-serving Prince of Wales; 's is read as 'has'

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means rising, so the word not is read upwards

explanation.surface: The prince refuses to stand up for the next dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns NOT upwards to TON, which follows CHARLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively 1920s ballroom step with swinging kicks is this named dance.

clue.text: Heartache about railway accident

indicators.note: the word for heartache goes around the railway letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain, as of heartache

explanation.surface: Grief following a train crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside PANG. PRANG is British slang for a car or plane crash.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a minor crash or collision of a vehicle.

clue.text: Agreement to attempt to restrict decay

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the word for attempt surrounds the decay word

parts.note: an attempt is a try
to decay is to eat away, as rust eats metal

explanation.surface: A pact aimed at limiting rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restrict' puts EAT inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal pact between nations is a signed accord.

clue.text: Orchestra leader subscribed to fast time for slow movement

indicators.note: subscribed means written below, so in this down clue the letter sits under the fasting season

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of orchestra

explanation.surface: The orchestra's leader signs up to a brisk tempo for a slow piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' means fasting, not quick: LENT. 'subscribed to' sets O (Orchestra's first letter) beneath it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning slowly, or a passage played at that tempo.

clue.text: Drawer has ugly row with poet

indicators.note: an ugly scene is a messy one, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist gets into a nasty quarrel with a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ugly' rearranges ROW and POET. 'Drawer' is not an artist but something that draws, that is pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope used for hauling a vehicle draws, that is pulls, what it is attached to.

clue.text: Ridiculous pretence of cleaner hoarding Ecstasy

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British cleaning lady
a hoarding is a billboard, which carries an ad
E is the street name for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cleaner pretends absurdly while stockpiling drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarding' looks like a container signal but is the British word for a billboard, giving AD. A CHAR is a British cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurd act put on to keep up appearances is a farce of this kind.

clue.text: Talk about item of clothing

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a hat is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: Discussing a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal conversation is a natter or gossip.

clue.text: Stumble in feeble illumination

indicators.note: the stumbling word is placed in the feeble word, inside it

parts.note: slight means feeble or flimsy
to stumble is to trip

explanation.surface: Tripping over in a dimly lit place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts TRIP inside SLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A long fluorescent tube light gives illumination to a room.

clue.text: Water swallowed very quietly in the throat

indicators.note: the water phrase takes in, swallows, the musical marking

parts.note: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for water
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: Water gulped down silently in the throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' puts PP inside ADAMS ALE (Adam's ale, water). The surface's swallowing fits the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bump of the larynx at the front of the neck sits there.

clue.text: Kipling's boy turned away from a party for Japanese emperor

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the boy's name reads backwards

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel Kim
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: Kipling's young hero is refused entry to a party thrown for the emperor of Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses KIM to MIK; then A and DO follow. 'away from' only joins the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English title used for the emperor of Japan.

clue.text: International players beat the tackle

parts.note: caps are players chosen for their national team
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: National team members thrash the opposition in a tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackle' is not a rugby move: it is ship's gear. A cap in British sport is a player chosen for the national side.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating drum on a ship for winding cable is part of the rigging gear.

clue.text: An uprising in the South Atlantic

definitions.meaning: an ascent or rising up, as of Christ into heaven
a remote British island lying in the South Atlantic Ocean

explanation.surface: A rebellion breaks out somewhere in the South Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' suggests revolt, but means going up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means rising upwards, and is also an island in the ocean between Africa and Brazil.

clue.text: Ed hated a fancy tie

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Ed loathed an elaborate necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges ED HATED A. 'tie' is a drawn race, not neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A race ending with two competitors level at the finish is a draw.

clue.text: Awe-struck conservationists sustain American patriot

indicators.note: to sustain is to hold up, so in this down clue the trust's letters support the patriot's name from below

parts.note: Paul Revere was the American patriot famed for his midnight ride
NT is the National Trust, Britain's heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Admiring environmentalists keep a hero of American independence going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sustain' puts NT under REVERE in the down entry. The National Trust (NT) preserves British historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deep respect and awe is being worshipful.

clue.text: Bob has to mess with one putting his foot down

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
to tamper with something is to mess with it

explanation.surface: Bob interferes with someone who insists firmly on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' is not a name: a bob was a shilling in pre-1971 British coinage, written s. 'putting his foot down' is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings a foot down heavily, literally rather than figuratively insisting.

clue.text: A soaking has Derbyshire openers stifling cry of pain

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the opening letters surround the cry

parts.note: the opening two letters of the county name Derbyshire, like a cricket team's two openers
ouch is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Derbyshire's opening batsmen get drenched and suppress a yelp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' gives two letters, as cricket teams send two openers in: DE. 'stifling' puts OUCH between them. Derbyshire is an English county with a cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet of water directed at the body is a drenching spray.

clue.text: It's clever getting spitfire to Land's End

parts.note: a spitfire is a fiery-tempered person, a shrew

indicators.note: the end of land is its last letter

explanation.surface: Flying a Spitfire to the tip of Cornwall is a smart move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spitfire' is not the plane but a hot-tempered person. 'End' picks D, the last letter of Land; Land's End is Cornwall's westernmost point.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and sharp-witted means smart in judgement.

clue.text: Police concealing redhead's body

indicators.note: the police word hides the letter inside it

parts.note: cops are police officers
the head of red is its first letter

explanation.surface: Officers hiding a ginger-haired person's corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts R (the head of red) in COPS. 'body' is a group, not a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit or organised group of people, such as an army division.

clue.text: Driving technique gets man and beast to Spain

parts.note: he is a man
an eland is an African antelope
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A fellow and his animal travel to Spain by car.
explanation.walkthrough: E is Spain's international vehicle registration letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing driver's method of working brake and throttle with one foot at once while changing gear.

clue.text: Measure one's alarm of Emily's pseudonym

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length
one is I, and 's is the contraction of is
a bell is an alarm

explanation.surface: Gauging an alarm set off by a pen name.
explanation.walkthrough: Emily Brontë published Wuthering Heights as Ellis Bell. The grid's second light reads SELL but the wordplay and the pseudonym need BELL.
explanation.definitionFit: The male pen name the Wuthering Heights novelist Emily Brontë adopted.

clue.text: Wager six-footer has energy

parts.note: an ant is an insect with six legs, a six-footer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tall man bets with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The stake put up before cards are dealt in poker.

clue.text: See 25
Figure, on reflection, electrical engineer concealed accident

indicators.note: the engineer letters hide the reversed word between them

parts.note: EE is the abbreviation for electrical engineer

indicators.note: reflection reverses an image, so the word for accident is read backwards

parts.note: a spill is a fall or accident

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, an engineer covered up a mishap, a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns SPILL to LLIPS, which 'concealed' puts inside EE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval shape is a geometrical figure.

clue.text: President to stay and be in authority

parts.note: P is a standard abbreviation for president; that the clue's word also begins with the full answer is a coincidence of the surface
to reside is to stay or live somewhere

explanation.surface: The president lingers on and holds power.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair or be in charge of a meeting or body.

clue.text: Floppy kites Ted designed

indicators.note: something designed is put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ted made some limp kites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges KITES and TED. 'Floppy' is not limp but a floppy disk.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy disk is a small removable computer storage disk.

clue.text: Space traveller having track in gym

indicators.note: the track word goes in the gym abbreviation

parts.note: PT, physical training, is school gym
a lane is a narrow track

explanation.surface: An astronaut does laps of the gym track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LANE inside PT. 'Space traveller' is a body orbiting through space, not an astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: A world orbiting a star travels endlessly through space.
